articles.prompt: Write about what do you feel when you write
articles.title: What writing makes me feel
articles.highlight: to love something is to let it matter to you
articles.body:
I don’t want to say it was a calling from the first day I came to know myself. Of course, I loved writing as a child. I wrote cringe love stories that were almost the same except for the characters. I also kept a diary for as long as I can remember, as a way to recreate ordinary days in my own way. But I didn’t know it is possible for me to be a writer.

I grew up in a small town where I wasn’t exposed to a lot of fields people could pursue in life or to much of the internet. I didn’t like TV either. So when I thought about writing, all I knew was being a broke artist who writes fiction and desperately hopes people like it.

I am good neither at being broke nor desperate, so I never seriously considered it. ‘I love words, so I will forever read them’ was how I was going about it.

Then one day at work (this is after graduation) we were given a book to read. It was “steal like an artist” by Austin Kleon. I was planning to start another book that day, so I was unhappy about it. When I saw the book, it was very short, so I just scanned through it that afternoon.

A week later, our managers started a discussion about it. I didn’t remember much about the book so I said, “I think the content is a bit small for a book. He could have just made it one episode of a podcast or an article. Why go through all the printing and the design of each page?”

(I apologized later when I reread it because the book is actually great. I just didn’t really sit down to read it.)

My manager was stunned. He called me rude and asked if I am a writer.

I almost choked.

“I try” I said with a nervous tone trying to look normal. 

With a straight face, he said, “you either write or you don’t. There is no such thing as ‘trying to write.’”

That day, I went home and kept thinking about why I almost choked. Why was it so scary for me to admit that I wanted to be a writer or that I write? Why did it feel like a weakness to want something for real? Why did letting something matter to me feel like being vulnerable?

I guess I was just scared that if I admitted to myself that I wanted to be a writer and never became one, I would forever feel like a loser. If something is important to me and I don’t get to make it happen, wouldn’t that make me a failure? 

So not officially wanting writing as a path was the safer option. To experience it a little without the pressure of actual commitment.

But I know that when I am in my 70s and someone asks me what I have been doing with my life, the less regretful answer will be, “I have been writing. I wrote. I am a writer.”
I was just scared I’d fail before I even took the first step.

So, to answer what writing makes me feel, it makes me feel weak I think. 

I feel weak when things go south and all I want to do is sit with a pen and paper and gossip with the ink. I feel scared when it works and I feel better after that. I feel intimidated when I come up with something to write and it feels bigger than who I am. When both writing and not writing about it seems hard.

I love writing. And to love something is to let it matter to you and to let things matter is to be vulnerable.

And that’s scary.

articles.title: My goal for the future
articles.highlight: writing makes living make sense
articles.body:
I have always thought my goal in life is very simple. Not easy or small, just simple. But because we usually think of goals as a list of things to accomplish, mine has always found a way to feel small compared to what most people aspire to or want from life. For many years, I felt like I lacked ambition. But that’s not true. I’m just ambitious about having a simple life.

I think the phrase “a goal for the future” is a bit generic. Because both 4 years and 40 years from now are in the future. But that’s what happens when we think of goals as a place to arrive or a thing to achieve. If we think of a goal as a lifestyle instead, I think we can come up with something that works for the future, whether that’s 4, 10 or 50 years from now.

My goal in life is simple, less regret and more contentment.

Visually speaking, it is a home filled with God, love, books and enough sunlight. Where I see myself is in a peaceful and quiet home where I don’t have a hard time falling asleep, wondering if I could have done life differently or better. My goal in life is a morning where I don’t wake up with a constant fear of what the day may bring and then rush through my ordinary days as a form of escape.

My goal in life is simple. It is to love people with the love of Jesus, be present to listen to people, make them feel seen and repeat.

It is to have a genuine connections that matters. Connections where we show up for one another on our good and bad days. Friendships that grow into our children becoming friends. Connections that hurt like hell God forbid, if we have to part ways for whatever reason.

My goal in life is simple. It is to do what I love and to love what I do.

My goal is to write every day. Not to make a living, but because  writing makes living make sense. I don’t like how the pressure of making a living can take the joy out of something (at least for me.) What I want is to create in order to understand myself or to inspire someone without feeling pressured into a cage called routine or unrealistic deadlines and unnecessary emails with corporate jargons.

The goal is a simple life, one full of God, love, books and sunlight. Less regret and more contentment. To love people and make them feel seen.

articles.title: Loving Someone
articles.highlight: anything done with genuine care and presence is love
articles.body:
There are different people I have loved throughout my life. There are also a lot of people I actively love right now. But that didn’t make writing this any easier.  I think love is something that is easier to do than to put into words. Not the simple “I love you” kind of expression, but defining what you actually mean by loving.

When I think about love, I think about one of my mother’s friends who once showed me a simple kindness by talking to me and asking about the things I cared about at a time when I felt like no one cared about my opinions or me. Thus, to love someone is as simple as listening to them.

When I think about love, I think about what me and my ex-best friend used to have. Communicating beyond words, always checking up on each other, buying them flowers just because and going to each other’s places to eat and talk. Thus, loving someone is being considerate, present and kind.

When I think about love, I think  about the birthday I broke down while talking to my sister over the phone and how she came to see me from afar right away, when she could have just kept trying to comfort me over the phone. Thus, to love someone is to show up when they’re breaking down and be with them.

When I think about loving someone, I think about my best friend and me. How we’ve maintained our relationship throughout the years though  we’ve gone through different changes in both of our lives. Thus, to love someone is to witness the different versions they become, grow alongside them and accept them with love again and again.

When I think about loving someone, I think about how my ex-best friend and I broke up and how it took me over 18 months to get over it. How everything about life hurt more in her absence and how it felt like I was dying at times. Thus, to love someone is to let them matter to you so much that when they leave, they strip and take away some version of you with them.

When I think about love, I think about the guy I once loved. How my values slowly started getting blurred throughout time, yet I convinced myself that he was worth it at the expense of everything. Thus, to love is to be dumb sometimes and to lose yourself too. 

I think loving someone is broad. Broad enough to encompass everything from the excitement in your smile when you spot them in a crowd to knowing their least favorite food. From sending them a cartoon character that looks like them to following up on that small and insignificant thing they mentioned about. It is asking if they’ve arrived home safe. It is being with them in the hospital when their loved one is admitted. 

Loving someone is too broad to fit into a note, or even a book for that matter. But I think we can say, anything done with genuine care and presence is love.

articles.title: Someone who inspires me
articles.highlight: I love watching her live. It inspires me.
articles.body:
I am not the kind of person who gets inspired by someone easily. I don’t think anyone is. I think being inspired takes watching someone’s journey for years and loving what you are being exposed to. So when I find someone who inspires me, I am grateful. I have few people who have been inspiring me throughout my life. One of them is Pomy (Mekdim) Hailu.

I first came across her on Facebook maybe seven years ago. She writes consistently  and I read almost everything she writes and ends up loving almost all of it. There is something about her words that makes me pause and become present in the moment. They take me out of whatever rush I was committed to and make me feel like I just remembered to breath after holding my breath for a minute.

I realized how much she inspires me recently, when I was feeling so discouraged about life and hating everything. After being away from Instagram for a while, I went back and there she was with her 17 stories a day :) I started reading not even her articles, but just her stories and immediately felt better. They were simple lines and very random that I don’t even remember what they were about. It was probably about how she had been smiling at her coffee so the coffee knows she drinks it because she wants to, not because she needs to or how she didn’t choose the day’s outfit, but let the outfit chose her.

Even though I love everything about her, her words are my favorite, of course. Especially when she writes about a place. Her words have the power to take me wherever she went and make me forget that I am sitting in an office with the email I drafted staring at me. 

As an aspiring writer, I know how hard it is to make someone feel fully included in the experience you are trying to express so my appreciation for her writing skills is beyond words. And one thing about following or knowing someone for so long is that you get to see the progress they make. I have watched her grow as a writer throughout the years and I am proud of her and it inspires me to write every day.

She is honest in a brave way. She is bold about whatever she believes in but says it with such gentleness and intentionality. She embraces the different experiences of being human and questions everything. From her own beliefs, to why something is named the way it is, to who created a certain social system we live in, she is curious and inquisitive about everything. For the mostt part she is busy with her interests, giving each day a chance to make its own kind of sense without forcing her meaning on it.

I can talk about her for a lot longer, but for now I will just say Pomy is the kind of human who makes me love being human a little more by loving her own life. I love watching her live. It inspires me.

articles.title: Your School
articles.highlight: Except he didn’t.
articles.body:
When I saw the word “school” what came to mind was not a structured timeline of me going to school, moving from one grade to another and coming back home. It was a collection of very random moments from my school years, most of which have nothing to do with the actual learning part. I’ll be honest, I don’t really like the past or things that belong to the past. But for this specific piece, I’ll try to go through some of the things I remember from elementary in a fun way I can.

—

I started school from Grade 1. I never went to nursery or kindergarten. Because I was the only one among my siblings who didn’t go to kindergarten, I always tried to make my father feel bad about it saying it is an abuse. I don’t know why they didn’t send me. They say there was no school close to home, and they didn’t want to send me somewhere far away.

Then, when I turned six, a new KG opened nearby and I got registered there. But because I was already reading and writing well, my dad thought I could manage Grade 1. So he took me there and when they accepted me, he convinced me to choose grade one saying that I would be ahead of my peers and that’d make me cool or something. Now the reality is the opposite. I always felt out of place because most of the kids were a year or two older than me.

Now, there are some shady things about how he got me accepted there. If you remember, you had to be able to touch your ears with your opposite hands to prove that you were seven. For weeks, I had been trying to touch my ears before the registration day as if trying would grow my hand longer in a week. I couldn’t make them touch without cheating a little, but my dad knew a teacher who convinced the people doing the registration and I got in(በዘመድ lol).

—


As a child, I was very scared kid.  I lived most of my life around avoiding getting yelled at. When someone tells me to do something, I don’t question it. I will just do it. I didn’t make a sound in class. I never missed homework. Students who were not obedient seemed like a completely different kind of creature to me because how could they handle someone scolding them like that?

As you know in elementary school, cleanliness is something that gets checked all the time(especially on Mondays). Because I almost never made mistakes in class, many of my teachers liked me. One of our science teachers used to call me “ቅመም”. One Monday, I went to school wearing a new t-shirt under my uniform coat. The t-shirt had a weird color that made it look like it hadn’t been washed in some places. The teacher started checking us. When it is my turn she looked at my hair, my nails and her eyes saw my t-shirt and she paused. 

She paused because she had never seen me have any issues with cleanliness before. She stared at it for a moment and said “ቅመም ምነው አንቺን ጎበዝ ነሽ ብዬ ለሰው ሁሉ ሳውራ የቆሸሸ ቲሸርት ልብሰሽ ትመጫለሽ?” It was my first time being in that kind of confrontational situation. I knew my t-shirt was clean but I couldn’t defend myself. I felt something hot on my cheeks and all of a sudden I was crying. She thought it was a mistake and I cried as an apology and she passed me without saying anything else.

—

There was a group of girls one batch above us whom I really admired from afar. Well, not so afar because whenever  there is school events, my friend and I would join them from our batch, but we weren’t that close either.Every year until Grade 5, I loved going to the International Children’s Day event which was celebrated on November 20. Students were selected to attend the events and some of them got to speak too. I was always the attendee but in Grade 5, I was selected to be a speaker and I was so excited. It was my first time writing something in English and I had it reviewed by someone whose English skills I trusted. I worked on my paper for a whole week staying late at night. 
 
When we got to the event, I was so excited about going up on stage and reading what I wrote that I couldn’t focus on anything else. Not the music, not the dramas, not the kids, not even the snacks and the candies. Then the time came. The MC called the chosen speakers from those girls one by one. The whole hall clapped at the end of the speeches as if it is the best piece they’ve ever heard and I got even more excited. Then my friend was called and went up and  I was the only one left. After her, I would be called. My heart started racing with both excitement and fear. My friend said her last line and got off the stage to a round of applause. I started getting ready to go up when the MC called my name.

Except he didn’t.

I don’t know what happened. He just called a representative from the Women, Children and Youth Office to give the closing speech. The lady spoke and the event was over. I was in shock. I don’t think I had ever felt rejection that painfully before. After the event, there were radio hosts covering the event and they were interviewing the kids who had presented their speeches. I was so sad that I didn’t get to present mine.

I think that was my last Children’s Day event I attended. I may have gone the next year, but I had lost interest in anything related to children and children’s day after that day.

——

These are just a few of the random moments I remember from my elementary school years. I wouldn’t say all of them, but most of the things I remember from the past don’t  make me feel good. Maybe that’s why I don’t like going back to it. I know that whatever happened in the past is connected in one way or another to who I am today and I am grateful for the ways my past has shaped me. But I also think it is possible to acknowledge the value of something without wanting to relive it through memories.

I know this piece feels unfinished and a little unorganized. But I think that is an honest reflection of how my mind works when dealing with the past. I don’t remember it as a neat timeline. I remember random moments, little details, feelings, people and things I probably haven’t thought about in many years. And that is okay.

articles.prompt: Something inspired of the 11th image on your phone
articles.title: Something inspired of the 11th image on your phone
articles.highlight: how much of human life is lived while waiting?
articles.body:
In a self help book I read some years ago, the author was talking about time. The time we spend in transportation specifically. He said that on average, a person spends three years of their life travelling and talked about how using some of that time to read or listen to audiobooks could positively affect the quality of our lives. Maybe that’s not exactly what he said, but that’s how I remember that section.

I don’t believe in hyper optimizing every minute of our lives but since then, I’ve started noticing how people spend the spaces in between transitions. How they spend their waiting. And because transportation is a kind of waiting we do to get somewhere we want to be, it is a good example. As someone who goes to work every morning through Addis traffic, I go through these tiny waiting seasons twice a day in a taxi and I use that time to observe.

I’ve noticed that people are always different in how they use their time while going somewhere. Some people talk on the phone for the entire journey with a friend and I can tell they’re the kind of person who doesn’t like being alone. I see it in how they instantly switch to TikTok the moment the call ends. I mean, are we not going to think about the conversation we just had for the last ten minutes?

Some people read. Some people just sit and think. I wonder what they’re thinking about. Maybe they’re having their alone time, trying to decide on that important thing they’ve been putting off. Some people talk and make temporary friendships with strangers. Some even sleep. Some are rushing without physically moving at all. Some are just sitting still.

Just like the people in the taxi, we have different places to go in life. Different journeys to make. Different versions of ourselves to become. Different stages of life to experience. Just like the people in the taxi, whether the journey is long or short, we have this space between where we are and where we are going. In the going, there is waiting. Waiting to get that somewhere.

I came across a line on Pinterest that said “How much of human life is lost in the waiting?”

A lot, I thought. A lot of human life is lost in the waiting. Not because waiting is necessarily bad but because often, waiting means being so focused on the thing we are waiting for that we don’t even notice that we are currently living in something we once waited for. Or we forget that waiting is also a stage that needs to be experienced.

I wonder what we do while we wait to get somewhere in life. While we wait to become this version of ourselves we desperately want to be. Do we try to make friends in that stage? Do we adopt something productive that belongs to that particular season? Do we rush through it until we’re done there? Do we hate where we are? Do we just sit still and wait? Do we do things just to kill time?

Oh, how I hate the term “killing time.”

Why kill time when we can make the time alive by doing things we actually like?

I’ve noticed that “killing time” is often the posture we have while waiting for things in life. We do nothing that feels significant enough to remember when we look back on that season. Or we rush. We rush as if the next big thing is always more exciting than the reality we already have in our hands.

Much of our life is lost in waiting because we are not taught how to make a life out of the waiting. We only know how to kill time while we wait.
Maybe if we learned not to be so focused on the things we are waiting for and instead learn to live fully through the things we once waited for, the now, the line wouldn’t have used the word ‘lost’ in relation to waiting.

Maybe the line would have been “how much of human life is lived while waiting?”

articles.prompt: Write about the lessons you’ve learned
articles.title: Write about the lessons you’ve learned
articles.highlight: Being right is overrated.
articles.body:
Since I didn’t do the ‘things I learned’ list for my birthday, I took today’s prompt as life giving me another chance to share the things I’ve learned. Yes, I’ve been learning a lot of things, but am I using those lessons to change my life for the better? that’s a topic for another time. But for now, here are some things (I remember) I’ve learned over the years that I think are worth mentioning, in no particular order.

Eating properly, sleeping well and staying hydrated are basic needs for a reason. Don’t deprive yourself of your basic needs. Don’t abandon your body. (I rehearse this to myself everytime I get sick lol)

Your natural inclination to assume things positively or negatively says something about you. Pay attention to the patterns and unlearn some of the useless assumptions your brain spends energy on unconsciously. I’d say don’t assume anything at all, but if you can’t help it, train yourself to assume things positively. I once saw a girl online say that she assumes everyone likes her unless they prove her  otherwise and I think adopting that kind of positive assumption about things is beautiful.

Be too much. In fact, there’s no such thing as being too much. Those who love you will keep loving you anyway. They will even applaud you for it. Those who don’t won’t suddenly love you because you refuse to take up space. They wouldn’t love you even if you became nonexistent. (I will have a lot more to say on this one day)

Changing your playlist from sad songs to happy ones helps a lot with your mood.

The idea of love you have in your mind is supposed to tell you something about your own loving patterns. You can’t use that to demand others love you the same way. People will love you the way they know how. You either have to teach them how to love you (which takes time, energy and work) or accept that their way of loving is different from yours.

“This is one of the marks of a truly safe person; they are confrontable.” 
— Henry Cloud
Don’t be afraid to confront people. You either get your answers or find out whether they’re safe people to have in your life. Both are a win.

Also, learn to be confrontable without getting defensive. Not everyone is trying to attack you. Most people confront you because they care about you enough to do so. Because it is easier to give up and shut down on someone than go ask them why they did things. 

Being right is overrated.

It’s not fair to expect others to accept parts of you that you have a hard time accepting yourself or expect others to love you when you don’t even love yourself.

Not every problem is yours to fix.

No one is going to reward you for going above and beyond for others at the expense of your own health. (Another thought I had while being sick) 

ጉድ አንድ ሰሞን ብቻ ነው

Love is all around you. You just have to open your eyes and be present.

You can’t keep outsourcing the connection you need to have with yourself to other people. Learn to become a good friend of yourself.

It’s not the end of the world to be a disappointment.

I heard this from Jay Shetty many years ago and found it to be so true “those who made you feel small at one point will never be part of your big life.”

The purpose of learning something about yourself is to unlearn what’s wrong and become a better person both for yourself and others. It’s not to just have the right language to justify your terribleness.

And lastly, it’s important to make space for whatever little things you learn to turn into wisdom. Live what you know. Knowledge you don’t put into practice is just you losing the privilege of being dumb in peace.

articles.title: A letter to someone, anyone
articles.highlight: I have become everything you wanted.
articles.body:
**Dear little me,**

I want to hope that this letter finds you well, but I know it won’t find you well. It can’t even find you because you don’t exist anymore. When people talk about the inner child and that kind of stuff, I always get confused. I know you don’t exist anymore. You’re gone, along with the unlived childhood I have such a hard time getting over. Thus I mourn you. Or I mourn for you. I don’t mourn you as a version of myself I once was but have now lost. I mourn you as someone close and dear to me who is gone. Someone outside of me. Someone different. When I look back to find traces of you and come across your little footprints, I don’t feel like you were me at some point. Maybe I am unintentionally denying you. Denying my past.

I don’t know if you want me to associate you with sadness, but sadness is what settles in whenever I think of you. I think that’s why I try my best not to think about you at all. Or deny you like I am not associated with you. I don’t want to think about you because what’s the point? I hate experiencing this sadness whenever I think of you. I hate that my heart breaks every time. It feels like a loss you never get used to.

I don’t want to think about you, but it seems you don’t care. You follow me around like someone who wants my pity. Or maybe I’m projecting onto you the only thing I know how to offer. Pity. Everything reminds me of you, as though you’re following me around. When I am in a good state, enjoying life and being at peace, I think about how you only survived and never got to enjoy your childhood. When someone makes me feel loved, I mourn the fact that you never felt safe enough to even understand what love was. I feel sad thinking about all those years you spent believing that love was just a manipulative stage in which the actors would eventually be punished for trusting it. That there is no such a thing as love.

When I make a mistake and feel disappointed in myself, I think about you. I blame what happened to you. Sometimes, I even blame you. Then I remember that you’ve been through so much and the last thing you need is me blaming you for being vulnerable. For being weak. For being a child.

Whenever it’s my birthday, it gets even worse because I always picture you sitting somewhere, minding your own business and pretending to be an adult. Just being silent, avoiding eye contact, ready to bite anyone who dares to get close like an angry little thing. I’m glad I have only a few pictures of you because at least most of the memories aren’t preserved on printed paper.

I don’t want to think about you. I don’t want the memories of you. But how sad is it that even I, who was you at some point, don’t want to sit through what you went through? How can we blame others for abandoning you when it took me years just to learn how to think about you? When I, someone who tries her best to be gentle with other people’s pain, don’t even want to look at yours?

I wish this was different. I wish I could help you out of wherever you are. I wish I could take away all the misery, bitterness and sadness and just help you be a child. I wish I could hug you. Or love you. I wish we could be friends. I wish I could have been there for you. I wish you could see who I have become. I have become that gentle and safe person you were always looking for. If someone like you ever found me, I promise they would feel safe. At home. I wil make sure they would experience the exact opposite of what you lived through. 

I have become everything you wanted. It is just sad I can’t be any of it for you.

articles.title: If we turned into days as we grew older, I hope I’d be Sunday
articles.highlight: Sunday is always kind enough not to run out too fast.
articles.body:
As a child, I wanted every day to go by fast so I could grow up quickly. I guess that’s what children do. They rush into adulthood, only to want their childhood back when they realize that growing up isn’t all they imagined it would be. You come to understand that it’s not where you are in life or how old you are that makes life better, but how you choose to live it. But as a child, I didn’t know that. I just wanted every day to be over. I would wake up wishing for the day to end. Though the days go by at a reasonable speed, the day called Sunday will never cooperate. Sunday is Sunday. It moves slowly, like it has nowhere to be. So I hated it.

As I grew up though, I grew into loving Sunday. It’s my second favorite day of the week now. The reason Sunday went from being my least favorite day to one of my most favorite is the same. Sunday is long. No one can convince me that Sunday has only 24 hours like the other days of the week. Sunday is like three days packed into one kind of long day.

I open the windows of my place and go out to buy something for breakfast. On my way, I get distracted by the trees swaying in the morning wind and stop to look at them. Then I notice their beautiful reflections moving on the black painted gate. I stare at them, mesmerized and try to capture a video. Then I put my phone away and just try to be there to witness it. I stand there for what feels like 10 minutes, only to realize it hasn’t even been 3.

I go to the kitchen to make breakfast, but first, I have to charge my phone. So I head to my bedroom, plug it in but I get distracted by a message I need to respond to from the night before. I end up scrolling for a while too. But when I check the time, Sunday morning is still fully here. Unlike other days, which seem to lose three hours when I spend thirty minutes scrolling, Sunday doesn’t rush off while I’m distracted.

So I make breakfast, get ready and go to church. After church, I wander around, meet friends, watch the kids play and take pictures of my friend’s kids. All of this feels like it should have taken a whole weekday, but it still is Sunday. 2:18 p.m to be specific. I usually come home with flowers because Sunday loves flowers, put them in a vase and stare at the floor until I get too hungry. I eat and fall asleep watching someone’s cleaning vlog. When I wake up, it is still Sunday. I can go for a walk, clean my place or just watch something. It’s still Sunday.

I love this routine because nothing is rushing me to get anything done. Even if I don’t do what I’m supposed to, I will probably still find time for it later in the evening because Sunday is always kind enough not to run out too fast. Unlike the other weekdays, which feel like money you’ve borrowed from someone and have to pay back, Sunday feels like it fully belongs to me and I can do whatever I want with it.

If I were to imagine the days of the week having personalities, Sunday would be that cool old guy who lives life slowly. Someone with intentionality. Someone mature. I can even imagine the rest of the week days going to him for advice whenever they’re going through something. He is kind and patient. When someone makes a mistake, he doesn’t instantly tell them to come back next week and leave. He smiles, says he understands and gives them another chance. Not next week, but this week. Today. This Sunday.  Sunday paces according to its own timeline and that timeline is usually slow and gentle.

articles.title: Write about love
articles.highlight: Is love even real if it needs a reason?
articles.body:
Ever since I read about the concept of fish love, I can’t help but keep thinking about how love is such a hard thing to do. That how much of what we call love everyday is a fish love. Fish love basically means, when I say I love fish, I am only talking about my preferred form of fish to eat, whether that’s salmon, fried fish or goulash. When I say I love fish, I am not saying I love to see a fish make friends in the ocean and swim happily in its natural environment. No, I mean that if I think it’s pretty, I will put it in a tank in my living room and watch it live in a cage every day because it makes me happy. It makes my place prettier. The fish is here for me. I love fish because it benefits me.

That made me stop claiming to love people so easily because much of what I call love is really just how much I love the way they love me. How much I love what they bring into my life. It is mostly about me. I see it everywhere too, in the way people love in real life, in the movies, in the songs. Recently, I came across Abraham Gebremedhin’s hankewutay song on the radio while I was on a taxi and I’ve been thinking about this section of the lyrics.

እንደጤዛ ህማይት እንደጉም
ጥልቅ ፍቅር አለሽ የሚኖር ዘላለም
አንቺ ነሽ ሃገሬም እናቴ
ሽልማቴ ርስቴ

የጠላሽ አይን ይጥፋ ሃገሬ
ስትኖሪ ነውና መኖሬ
ጉዳት በደለሽን አያሰየኝ ባይኔ … እያለ ይቀጥላል

Do you see how the deep love that lives forever within him is tied to what his country offers him? Every expression of love seems to come with a reason. A place to live. A community he has built his identity around. A source of safety and survival. I am not judging him at all because my own way of loving is no better but የጠላሽ አይን ይጥፋ ምክንያቱም ስትኖሪ ነውና የምኖረው sounds to me like he is talking less about his love for his country and more about how much he needs it to survive.

Since I read about fish love, the whole concept of love has started to feel like a chore. When someone tells me they love me, I want to ask why and listen very carefully as they explain. But more importantly, when I feel like I love someone, I ask myself why. Why this person and not another? Would I still love this person if they didn’t possess these qualities? Would I still be friends with them if they weren’t the way they are? Is love even real if it needs a reason?

I don’t know whether loving someone and wanting them around because they posses certain quality is right or not. Part of me thinks that’s just how we are as humans. We see the world through the lens of how it relates to us. We love or hate, appreciate or condemn, depending on how things affect us and that's fine.

Another part of me says love should be free. Free from needs and expectations. 

I once saw someone talk about why she adopted a cat on instagram. She said “people say ‘cats are selfish and not loving enough and that they’ll leave you for a piece of better comfort’ but that’s the exact reason why I love cats. My cat teaches me to love without expectations”. I thought that was interesting.

If I love someone, it should be because I choose to love them, not because I need them in my life (at least ideally). Maybe that sounds like I’m denying the fact that we are relational creatures and love sustains our need for connection. But that’s not what I mean, I just want relationships to exist without the pressure of having to offer something. I want to be able to love someone without making their presence in my life conditional on what they bring to it.

If there were an imaginary perfect world where nothing was lacking, where I didn’t need anything from anyone, I would still want to love the people I claim to love.

articles.title: Your celebrity crush
articles.highlight: I regret not doing it.
articles.body:
I don’t remember ever having a celebrity crush. Maybe I am not exposed to the media enough to catch feelings for someone from that far away. Maybe I never study celebrities beyond the characters or the music they play. Even when I like someone, my feelings stay attached to the character they played, not the person behind it. If it is a song, it stays about the song. I guess that’s because I am not that into how people look. Cebebrities for me are usually just good looking.

I am the kind of person who sees someone and thinks “Yeah, this is the person I am going to marry.” I might not know anything about this person and they might not even be conventionally attractive but I will just look at them and decide that I am attracted to them. I don’t fully understand how that works yet, so I have been trying to learn more about attraction.

I think having a crush is fun, especially when you have time. These days, I feel like I am too old for it. Even calling a feeling as a crush comes with a weird feeling. When I was on campus though, I used to have crushes all the time. I had this bad habit of developing a crush around finals so I could justify not studying by telling myself I was heartbroken. Looking back that was so dumb.

Having a crush was fun. Our dorm used to be so much fun because of it. Whenever someone had a crush on someone, we all got invested in the story. It was the highlight of our days. We even had this habit of collecting things from our crushes as artifacts and hung them in the room. I don’t know who came up with that idea, a water bottle from someone, a chocolate from another person, someone’s handwriting…

One day, a friend from another dorm came in and saw all the things hanging. She asked what they were. One of the items was a water bottle with a little water left in it, which she thought was ጸበል. We told her it was from one of our crushes and she was disturbed.

“ይሄ ጠንቋይ የሆነ ዶርም” ብላ ሄደች 

There was also a teacher one of our friends had a crush on and we all got good grades in his course. After class, whenever we saw his car parked, we would visit the car and talk about leaving a letter on it. Imagine how fun that would have been, but we were scared, we didn’t do it. I regret not doing it. What was the worst that could have happened? He was a gentleman. The worst he could have said was, “Thank you, but no.” But us, we could have had a story to laugh about for the rest of our lives. 

I think the last time I had a crush, I was grown up enough not to make a big deal out of it. But there was an opportunity for us to meet through work, so I arranged things in a way that allowed us to work together. We did and he turned out to be mediocre when it came to the final product. And just like that, the crush I had flew away.

This was an ordinary person by the way, not a celebrity.

Yeah, celebrity crushes. I have never had one and I don’t really understand them either. A celebrity is a celebrity. He most probably doesn’t even know I exist. If he isn’t Ethiopian, he might not even know whether Ethiopia is a city, a town, a country or a continent. And to be honest, I think the probability of me becoming a celebrity is way greater than the probability of me ending up with one so I am glad I don’t get crushes from celebrities.

articles.title: My first love
articles.highlight: That’s how I survive, I guess. By forgetting.
articles.body:
I don’t like the past, for the most part. I don’t like going back to it. It’s not that I don’t know how much the past has contributed to the life I claim to love now. I do. I just want to appreciate the life I have without ever having to go back and revisit what happened before it.

My first love is one of the reasons. Well, 'my first relationship', as I would like to call it. There’s a part of me that cringes at the thought of calling what happened between us love. I want to look back on it with generosity and leave it as something good or at least as an experience but my body doesn’t cooperate at all. It cringes. Instead when I think about it, my brain gets technical about it and explains away why it wasn’t love but just two kids who didn’t know how to deal with their feelings, getting confused together and hurting one another.

We met at school. I had known him since grade 5 or 6, but we didn’t become friends till grade 11. Grade 11 was the year something big happened in my life, something that affected me deeply and not in a good way. I didn’t have many friends and I didn’t know how to talk about serious things, so at some point, I even stopped going to school. We used to chat around that time, so he reached out to me. I told him I was having a hard time and he came to see me that day. I really needed to talk about what happened, so I told him. We talked about it and things seemed to get better afterward. I got back to school again.

We became close after that and he adopted me into his friend group, almost all his friends became my friends. Whenever I think about him, these are the two good things that come to mind. He cared enough to come and see me and talk to me about what had happened during one of the darkest times in my life and he shared his friends with me.

How we got together was funny, though. We had started spending time together and meeting almost every day and one day, I became confused about where things were going. So I asked him. I said “it seems like we’re more than friends, what are we really?” (because your girl could use some clarity).

He was offended. He was so offended that I didn’t know we were in relationship, that I had to calm him down and pretend I already knew, that I asked only because I wanted to make sure, when in reality the whole thing was news to me. A big news. That was the people pleaser in me, unable to stand the thought of someone being mad at me. And just like that, I was in a relationship.

We stayed together for two years, which is a long time. I used to wonder what my life would have looked like if I had never gotten into that relationship, or into relationships at all. Now looking back, I know the last thing that version of me needed was a romantic relationship. What I needed was a friend. Someone better than me at navigating life, someone who could be there for me, guide me without any romantic involvement. But he wasn’t better than I was so we both got lost together even more.

I came across a relationship dynamic in a book called “The subtle art of not giving a f*ck” by Mark Manson that made me understand what we had. One person avoids dealing with their own problems, while the other likes dealing with everyone’s problems except their own. When these two people come together, they are match made in heaven, because each person’s behavior enables the others. The person who avoids their problems gives the other person something to focus on. While the person who likes fixing everyone else’s problems gets to feel important and useful in the relationship, while also avoiding their own problems.

He didn’t like dealing with his problems and I didn’t like dealing with mine. So I took on his problems to avoid dealing with my own. That’s how we managed to stay together for two years. The thing about dealing with other people’s problems for too long is that eventually, you’ll become resentful. Because resentment is a sign that you are carrying something that is not yours carry. And I was becoming so resentful.

I also had issues communicating my needs, so instead of telling him when he hurt me, I silently kept track of everything at the back of my head. I let it build up until one day, I had enough. I finally told him about the things he had been doing, maybe for the past year or more. He was hurt by the fact that I had been pretending everything was fine when in my head, it clearly wasn’t. 

Our relationship had always felt suffocating to me. But at the time, I didn’t know what it felt like to breathe right, so I didn’t know I was suffocated. I never felt considered. I never felt like I mattered. He never felt understood. I know I’m being vague here but getting into the specifics would make it sound like I’m blaming him for everything, when we were both responsible for what happened. We tried to fix things, but by then, I had already checked out mentally.

It was also clear that we would never end up together. He was Muslim and I was a Protestant Christian. I wasn’t strong in my faith or even very concerned about religion at the time that made him assume that I would eventually convert without talking to me about it. I remember one day I was so angry. I had had enough of feeling like I wasn’t being considered and him making decisions for me without even asking what I wanted.

I don’t remember exactly how the conversation started, but at some point, he said something like “when you convert…” and continued with his line as if he wasn’t talking about something that would affect my life in a huge way.

“When did I say I would convert to muslim, why did you assume that?” I asked.

He shamelessly said “if you’re not going to convert, how is this going to workout?”

So I was the one who had to compromise. I was so angry that day. I went home and not long after that, as if that wasn’t enough, he asked me whether I would be okay with him marrying another woman after we got married. Bro knew what he wanted out of life at that age (except he’s not even married to one person yet, let alone two lol). It was at that moment that I knew I …

There was also this time when he told me he wanted us to get engaged before we left for campus. I said no. He seemed he agreed, yet he proposed anyway on my birthday, with a lot of our friends watching. He knew the people pleaser in me wouldn't let me say no, so I got engaged on my 18th birthday. Now thinking about it, it is embarrassingly funny (the people pleaser in me could have had me married btw, because I also once said yes to another relationship I didn't want because I didn't know how to say no 😂)

I should have said no, but I didn't. I couldn’t bring myself to end things right away. When we went to campus, though, the distance between us became obvious enough that he understood where things were heading. and eventually, we ended it.

The cruelty of the past is that you can look back at it, see what happened and can do nothing about it. You can only regret your past. You can’t change a thing. I was hurt. A LOT. I lost so much and it didn’t even come with the experience of love that would make me say it was worth losing those parts of myself. The more I learned about relationships and how things should have been, the sadder I became because it was just that bad. 

So I convinced myself that it was better to forget the whole thing as though it had never happened. And I did. I don’t feel anything when I think about it. I don’t even feel like it’s part of my story anymore. That’s how I survive, I guess. By forgetting.

articles.title: Thirty facts about myself
articles.highlight: Exiting through an entrance will haunt me for weeks.
articles.body:
1. I am not as self aware as I think I am
2. I have unapproachable serious resting face that says ‘get near and I will bite you’ but when you get near what you get is a smile. 
3. Most of my life is a result of coincidence because I am not a planner but somehow, I like where my life is going
4. Thinking the worst about things makes me feel I am in control because nothing bad gets me by surprise.
5. I am not competitive for the most part, if I ever am though, it is usually with someone 20+ years older than me who has their life figured out in ways I haven't figured mine out yet.
6. I am not into trends at all, I don’t get them.
7. I have hard time acknowledging my achievements, even saying my achievements makes me feel weird. 
8. Deep deep down, I am lover. I love loving on people. I think humans are so beautiful and lovable.
9. I have a lot to learn about friendships and relationships in general.
10. I am one of those people who falls in loves with a single song from an album and listens it non stop
11. I used to know every line of the poem in the book ፍቅር እስከ መቃብር and recite it to myself. I still remember a lot of it.
12. I am way more scared of failing than I would like to admit 
13. Coffee makes me sick, but is coffee sick of me? No. So I keep having it sometimes.
14. I am afraid of heights and flies. I plan to go skydiving one day to face my fear of heights, but as for flies, I'd like to live in a world without them.
15. I might have an anger issues. 
16.  ብዙ ነገር ወተት ነጭ ነው ካልተባለ አይገባኝም
17. Scrolling is my coping mechanism for stress, I could scroll for 10+ hours straight if I am stressed.   
18. I am obsessive without discipline, so I usually end up dedicating myself/my time to things I shouldn't.
19. I love the smell of the morning and I hate the energy of midday 
20. I try to follow every rule. Exiting through an entrance will haunt me for weeks.
21. I love asking questions, even though they usually end up making me feel a fool or a weirdo.
22. I want to make sure every step of my life is in line with God's plan because I am obsessed with getting it right.
23. I take way more responsibility for everything than I should. 
24. I get sad easily about almost everything, but I don't get happy as easily.
25. I usually realize I am in danger after I got myself into a danger
26. I don't have a favorite book, song, color, place, or anything . It all depends on the moment.
27. I am actually very flexible and open to changing my mind when I realize I am wrong. It doesn't take much convincing once I see it.
28. My default expectation is that people will disappoint me. It doesn't surprise me much when people are bad, it surprises me when they're good. 
29. I grew up romanticizing being a single mom (I don't know what or who influenced me), but now it is one of my biggest fears.
30. It has taken me a lot of years and energy and disappointments to unlearn the people pleasing habit I used to have

articles.title: Ways to win my heart
articles.highlight: their words do the work
articles.body:
One thing this daily writing prompt is making me realize is how unaware I am of myself. Every prompt feels like I am being asked to write about a stranger. I took my notebook with me today to write wherever I end up, but I wrote nothing. I thought about it for the whole day, but there wasn't much I could recall. Does this mean my heart has never been won, lol. I don't think so. I think I have just never been intentional about noticing what makes me feel a certain way about people or why certain encounters stay with me, instead I have just been enjoying having my heart won. 

It's a good thing I now know that, because from now on, whenever someone starts having a special place in my heart, I will ask myself why and keep track of the things that got them there. For now, thinking about the things the people who have a special place in my heart have in common, I have come up with a few ones.

The first one is consideration. When someone is considerate, whether towards me or others, I just can’t help but notice and starts to delight in their existence. Not the kind of consideration that is merely for show, but the kind that comes naturally to people who are genuinely considerate. How beautiful is it to think beyond yourself and consider the people around you? How beautiful is that person who checks whether everyone has arrived home safe after a group meetup. That person who brings little treats just because. Someone who remembers details and make them feel special with it. The person who plans someone else's birthday. Someone who shares their connections with you when you need them without even thinking twice, because helping out is simply in their nature. I have a huge admiration for these kinds of people. 

Another way into my heart is when someone is just themselves.

I used to think I liked people who felt comfortable to be around, people who were similar to me. Then I met people who were completely opposite to me. Every encounter with them makes me uncomfortable, yet they still could have a special place in my heart and I love them dearly. It's not about whether they are quiet or chatty, it is not that whether their aesthetic is my type or not, it is not even about whether they always make me feel a certain way. What draws me to them is when they are simply in their own world, sounding like themselves, however weird or cringey they might sound. People who are unapologetically themselves, who are doing their own thing and are busy living life their own way, inspire me to do the same. And I can't help but let my heart be won every time I encounter them.

Last but not least are people who are good with words and know how and when to use them. This one has more to do with me than me watching them have that effect on others, because everyone has a different view of what a good word means. 

If you are a deep thinker who can explain things with beautiful words, I will listen as if you are reciting poetry. I believe that when you are good with words, conversations become less like a normal conversations and more like sharing a good food. Reading the words of those kinds of people, listening to them speak or even watching them express themselves feels like attending a live art performance without a crowd. I especially love these people because, unlike with the first two, where I am usually the one who makes a place for someone in my heart, these people builds a place for themselves with their words. I just have to be around them and their words do the work. 

These are just some of the qualities that grip my heart, earn a place in it and stays.

articles.title: Someone I miss
articles.highlight: love can also be quiet
articles.body:
I searched for what missing means to make sure I am on the same page as everyone about what it actually means. My search result said missing someone is “a mix of longing, an aching void and nostalgia. It happens when a familiar presence or pattern is suddenly absent from your daily life.” Longing and an aching void sounds a beautiful way of putting it.

I know this feeling. I am not someone who experiences missing people very often, but I have experienced that feeling with a couple of people before. But now, I am at a point in my life where I don't miss anyone. I have sat long enough, trying to feel the absence of someone in my life, but no one came to mind. I am not longing for anyone or feeling an aching void at all. Which made me question whether I love anyone at all if I am not missing them. 

Is it possible to love people and still not miss them when they are no longer here? To share moments you treasure like a meaningful gift, to laugh with genuine joy over silly things, to go to coffee shops and talk for six hours and still not want those moments back?

Well, not exactly not wanting them back, because I do want to see these people again, of course. I do want to relive those moments someday hopefully. But wanting to see someone and missing them are not the same thing. For me, by wanting I mean remembering people as something good that I want to encounter someday again. It is not a longing or an aching void. Not yet, at least. I have always struggled with this question, why can't I miss people? Because missing someone is usually associated with love, I feel this pressure to be sentimental when it doesn't come easily or naturally to me.

And then other times, I wonder if I have been measuring my love by the other people's standards. Maybe I have been looking only for the ache instead of paying attention to the affection. Maybe I have been waiting for the absence of someone to make itself known in a way that I can recognize, forgetting that love can also be quiet. It can be in the joy of sharing a meal, in the conversations that stretch for hours without either person noticing the time. These things have happened in my life a lot of times and I was grateful for them. Why then do I need to feel a void afterward for those moments to count?

I think part of the reason is that the extreme romanticization of missing people. A lot has been written about it, songs are made about it and at some point it has become an evidence of how much someone means to us. There is something beautiful about longing for someone, about carrying their absence with you. But I feel like we have made missing someone the only significant part of loving them that we hid the other ways of loving people.

When most people carry their love through longing, through that aching void, there are people like me who carry it through remembring it and just being grateful for it.

articles.prompt: If you could run away, where would you go?
articles.title: If you could run away, where would you go?
articles.highlight: Home. I’d run away to home.
articles.body:
The first thing that came to mind was, I don’t know. Because if I knew where the place I want to be was, I could have been gone by now. I don’t know where it is located. I am not even sure it exists at all. It is an imaginary world I used to escape to, a place where I could find refuge from reality. But growing up taught me how much it hurts when reality slaps your imagination through its persistent existence which made me afraid to run away, even in my imagination. Imagination is supposed to be something reality catches up to someday, but in my case, my imagination caught up with reality and here I am.

It has been a while since I last went to that place, but from what I remember of my previous visits, it felt like a safe haven. It is quiet. So quiet that you can almost hear your heartbeat, and your unintentional, harsh breath sounds like a loud noise. But it is not the kind of quietness you cannot wait to escape, or the kind that scares you. The quietness is comforting and the eeriness is familiar and safe. Because the place is safe.

It is somewhere I don’t have to recite my lines before saying what I want to say for fear of being misunderstood. It is somewhere I don’t have to silently wish for certain topics not to come up because, here, I can say I don’t want to talk about something without my voice getting nervous. Here, I don’t have to work my way into being accepted by people who don’t like me, because I know how to comfortably live with it.

In this imaginary, perfect, quiet place, I don’t spend so much of my time grieving what could happen because I am content with what is. It is somewhere I don’t struggle for control because I have learned to relax amidst the waves of life. If I could run away, I would. I’d run somewhere I could rest without feeling like I was falling behind, somewhere my brain didn’t have 20+ tabs running at the same time and somewhere so beautiful that I’d forget I own a device with a screen.

If I could run away, I’d run somewhere people are always my people, the food doesn’t taste like adulthood caught me by surprise, and the mornings are always longer than the rest of the day. If I could run away, I would go somewhere where hurt doesn’t stay longer than we agreed it could, love is not selfish, honesty is the language, goodbyes are only for eight hours of sleep and hugs are always warm and alive. 

If I could run away, I would go somewhere safe.

Home. I’d run away to home.

In people and sometimes in a place, I am looking for a home to go to. But I don’t know where this quiet and perfect home is located. 

So, to answer the question, home but I don’t know where that home is located.

So I don’t know.

articles.title: Describe your style
articles.highlight: simple, neutral, but cute
articles.body:
If we’re talking about fashion style here, I’d say this prompt was probably developed by someone white or someone who isn’t from sub sahara. Because I don’t think many people here are particularly concerned with having a defined style, or at least one they can describe as their signature style. But since I didn’t do my research well on the prompt before posting, I’ll write about it anyway.

As a child, I really admired my older sister’s style. I don’t know if it was just the whole thing about being obsessed with your older sibling and thinking they’re the coolest person alive, or if her style was really that interesting. I grew up watching her, and I loved everything about how she presented herself. How she styled her hair, applied her makeup, chose her outfits. I loved everything she owned and silently wished I could be like her when I grew up. I was the happiest whenever she gave me her clothes. I felt so confident wearing them, and now that I think about it, most of them weren’t even my size. I’m sure I looked like I was wearing borrowed clothes at the very moment I felt the most confident. She has been a major influence on my fashion sense, which is interesting because her style has changed quite a lot over the years. She’s no longer the version of herself I watched and admired as a child, but I think I’m still stuck on that version of her.

Her style was simple for the most part. Nothing dramatic, nothing bold or experimental. It felt as though she preferred not drawing too much attention to herself, so she mostly went for neutral colors and simple outfits. I copied her and developed a similar style of my own. I don’t like wearing things that draw too much attention, so I too have mostly been about playing it safe.

I’ve always admired people who wear bold things and experiment with their appearance. I even assume they must be cool just because they’re brave enough to wear things I wouldn’t. I’m not brave enough to wear something that doesn’t look normal to me, yet. I think fashion shouldn’t come at the expense of comfort, so I’ve mostly stuck to what feels comfortable. Besides, everything in life is uncomfortable so the least I can do is make myself comfortable in what I wear, however boring and unbrave that might look and feel. 

So, simple, neutral, but cute. That’s how I’d describe my style.
As the usual Pinterest obsessed person, I have several saved boards dedicated to outfits, makeup, and hairstyles. If anyone would go through them one by one, it wont take them much time to notice the similarities of it all. Simple, neutral, and cute.

articles.title: Favorite book
articles.highlight: books are like strangers I meet in public
articles.body:
I love books. I love the shape of a book, how it is full of words that only make sense when I read them in an orderly manner, and how experiences leave their footprints there. Though I don’t read as much as I want to, I love books, and there is no denying that. I am grateful books exist. I also admire the commitment of the writer behind every book, whatever the book is about. As someone who discovered books as an escape at first, that is what they remained for as very long time, a way to outsource the experience of life with the help of someone else’s words. Books were the only way I experienced life. I was too scared to go out and live, so I used them as a safer way of living.

But as I grew up and became wise enough to understand the reason for my obsessions with reading, I confronted myself that I couldn’t always live under the idea of life but had to go out and make the actual life happen for me. Since then, I haven’t been reading much. Books are now for entertainment and learning purposes. I say entertainment, but there is not much time when a book has left me entertained. Books usually make me think, doubt, overthink and stress and that’s what I have been calling entertainment. And I think because how stressed almost everything I read leaves me, as much as I love books, I don’t get attached with a single book. 

I get confused about which book to name every time someone asks me what my favorite book is. Favorite as in like a favorite snack I go back to again and again? It would make me a liar to say I have a favorite book in that way because I don’t usually return to books after I’ve read them. As much as I enjoy one book, there are still so many others I need to read and there is never enough time. Life is already too short to read every book once let alone twice.

But if we define favorite by its impact, I would say almost every book I read impacts me in a different way. I am the kind of person who believes every book has something to offer and so far, everything I have read has impacted me in some way. I find a thought in one book, a question in another, an idea in another, or a strange story that happened somewhere and leaves me with a different perspective on things. So I don’t know how to have a favorite book in this context too.

If it is about what comes to mind when I hear the question, it is usually the book I am currently reading or have read recently. I fall in love with every book I sit with and connect with it so deeply like there was no other book that made me feel the way I do now. But with time that slowly fades as I proceed to the next book.

All this is to say that I don’t really have a favorite book. It must be unbelievable coming from someone who talks about books and wants to write one someday, but I don’t. While writing this, I tried approaching the question from different ways and even considered mentioning some books I remember liking. But why stress over things when I can simply be honest about. And the honest answer is that I don’t have a favorite book.

I read a book, I like it, I think about it, I put it back and it ends there. When I am having a conversation and I think a book has something to offer in that situation, I might suggest it. Or, if I am writing a review, which I am trying to do more often to document my learning, I might end up recommending it with reasonable explanations. Other than that, books are like strangers I meet in public. Rarely do we cross paths again. I admire the wisdom, appreciate the art and the person behind it and still move on without tagging it as a favorite or not favorite.

—

With that being said, I am currently reading the autobiography of a man named Kieth McNally titled “I regret almost everything.” I haven’t finished it, I am not even halfway through but so far I love it and it is my current favorite.

articles.title: This is Us
articles.highlight: everyone learns how to be human for the first time
articles.body:
I don’t remember who suggested it to me or how I discovered it. I just remember starting “This Is Us” one weekday morning after breakfast during covid break. It would not be an exaggeration to say I fell in love with all the characters right away. It was interesting how everyone existed for a convincing reasons, not because anything about them was extraordinary, but because their lives and connectedness to one another made sense in the same way the lives of people around us in real life make sense. 

The coincidences felt very natural. Someone meets someone at work, they become friends, grow into love only to discover something that makes it impossible for them to be together. Someone grows up watching his alcoholic dad and struggles with the same problem but wants to do better for his family. Someone’s parents disapprove of a guy because he is broke. It all just makes sense.

I loved the couples so much at first. Their love felt ordinary, realistic and safe. Because the storytelling moved between the present and the past, I enjoyed the past more because, well, the guy was only alive in the past. What started out as a story around two young couples slowly expands to include their families, their kids, their kids’ spouses and friends and their spouses’ family, and it sort of becomes a community of people. As the story involves more people and introduce more new characters, I loved how the new characters never became just side characters. It was as if the story wasn’t about one particular person or group of people, but about everyone. Everyone who comes into the lives of the main characters has their own life, their own moment, they get to live as their own person, not as a side character and leave when needed.

Once, while talking about it with a friend, she told me she thinks everyone on the show was so beautiful. Beautiful not in physical appearance, though that might be the case for some of them, but in how they held their humanity. How honest each character was. Their weaknesses, their wins and their struggles were all relatable. There is no villain in the story. Everyone is justified in why they act the way they do. They’re just living their lives and dealing with the friction that happens between them, as everyone learns how to be human for the first time.

No problem is extraordinary and I’d believe them if someone tells me something like this had happened somewhere in the world. There is sadness, happiness, family, love, learning, sacrifice, regret, someone doubting their worth, someone struggling with addiction, someone dealing with loss, someone comparing themselves to someone else, someone trying to lose weight, someone trying to have a baby, someone learning to be a parent, someone trying to have a good time, someone drowning in depression, someone failing many times and trying to get back up…. Maybe the show has portrayed it beautifully with the storytelling, but this is just what I think life is like and I don’t think life is any crueler or softer than this for an ordinary person.

The storytelling was beautiful, as it naturally wove together the present and the past without you even noticing the transitions. I loved watching these people because I connected with almost everyone in different ways. I also loved that I couldn’t guess or feel the pressure to guess what would happen next because it would be me trying to guess what would happen next in life. The way the story unfolded was ordinarily unexpected. I remember crying at one point and I don’t usually cry. Dramatic me also had hard time accepting some losses that the characters seemed to accept so well.

You know I have issues with the word favorite. It has an uncomfortable weight for me to claim something as favorite. It has also been years since I watched it, so part of me wonders if I would still enjoy it as much as I did then, or if I have changed enough that I wouldn’t enjoy it the same way anymore. But at the time, I was obsessed with it. I was so obsessed. And I haven’t watched another series since then so, let’s say “This Is Us” is my favorite series so far.

articles.title: Talk about your sibling
articles.highlight: she is my person
articles.body:
We grew up with people calling her የፍቅር ሰው. I thought that was weird. One, because I was never the affectionate one. Two, because የፍቅር ሰው is a bit too long to be a name. It is a phrase. People would see us together and of course say “እውነትም የእናት ሆድ ዥንጉርጉር ነው”. But now that I think about it, how beautiful is it to be so loving that people stop using your actual name and call you የፍቅር ሰው instead? Love was in her blood. She loved everyone and she loved loving. She still does. 

If she loves everyone and loves to love, imagine how she loves and treats me. Even though I am the older one, I am usually the one who always gets spoiled. (Some of my friends compare their siblings to her and use her as the standard for how a sibling should be loved 💅🏽)

She is my best friend. She is the first person I go to when I am sad and she is usually the only person who notices my mood swings over the phone, listens to me and sits through my unusual, weird obsessions too. She calls me constantly to check up on me because only God knows how I am doing at any moment. She loves me so well and I don't know how I can love her back the same way. She is one of the reasons I see how God has favored me. She makes the concept of unconditional love make a little more sense in a human context. Yes, there is a condition of us being siblings and growing up together, but i'd say she loves me more than a sibling normally would and she loves me the way I want to be loved. (Am i making this about me ende 😭)

Everything is funny with her. We always laugh until our bellies hurt, until people at the next table roll their eyes at us if we're out because we're always laughing. And in all those moments of laughter that hurts, I feel what a blessing it is to have a sister and best friend in one person. Also, our birthdays are on consecutive days and I see that as a wink from God about the two of us.

Growing up was a different story though. We always, constantly fought. They say siblings, especially those close in age, fight a lot. Ours was a bit more than a lot. I remember our dad building an extension room beside the house and moving out because of us. His reason? “እኔ ክስራ ደክሞኝ ስመጣ የነዚህን ሴቶች ጭቅጭቅ አልቻልኩትም.” To this day, I wonder if we were really that unbearable or  if he was just being dramatic. Because we were kids, probably twelve and ten. 

Everything we fought over was silly. For example, when we were reading, she would read out loud or hiss the words under her breath and I can't concentrate on mine. She knew how to annoy me well. Or we would sit together so I can help her study, but I had no patience, so we'd end up fighting. Other times, it was laziness. We were both so lazy that whenever we were told to do something, we'd start listing everything we had done over the past weeks to prove that it should be the other person's turn.

I also hated it when she touched my stuff. Especially my clothes, because she always brought them back ruined in someway. The sad part about this is that she was always willing to give me everything she had, but because I didn't want to share anything of mine, I never asked to borrow hers. I think I traumatized her with my constant “don't touch my stuff” so much that even after we grew up, even now, she gets surprised when she likes something of mine and I tell her to take it. She also stresses a lot if she accidentally broke or ruined something of mine.

We weren't friends as kids and I think I was the problem. As an older sister, if I had been more patient and loving, things might have been different because she was full of love. We have pictures of her attempting to kiss me while I move away uncomfortably because I don't like kisses. But she tries to kiss me every single time we take pictures.  I feel like I deprived her of love as a child. I try to compensate that time and she gets so happy when I kiss her or tell her I love her.

It is after I left for campus, we started having a special connection. We started talking. We started becoming friends and with her loving me unconditionally I started feeling safe enough to open up. With time, we became the bestest of friends. The older I get, the more grateful I become for her every day. Not just because she is my sibling and we are connected by blood, but because she is my person.

And I hope we'll grow old like this and still be laughing in our seventies the way we do now. I hope we'll always stay best friends.

articles.title: Your best friend
articles.highlight: He just kept loving me.
articles.body:
You might not remember where and how a friendship with someone you call your best friend started. Or you might. But whether you remember it or not, it is rare for a friendship to begin with you breaking down to the point of death in front of the other person. Or let’s say it did. It is even rarer for the stranger you broke down in front of to take you into his world and for a friendship to grow out of it. But that’s just how it started. I broke down, he took me into his world and that friendship became the best thing that has ever happened to me.

Shortly after we met, we started meeting every day. I needed that kind of connection in my life. Someone who would just be there. Someone who would talk to me. Someone who would love me just for me. Someone who see me for the broken person I was and still wants to be friends. Someone who wouldn’t be scared away by my problems. Someone safe. Someone who listens. Someone who accepts me when I had a hard time accepting myself. Someone who shows up through every circumstance of life. And most importantly, someone who does all these things without expecting anything in return. Someone who didn’t need me but still wanted me anyway.

Such generous kindness was as strange to me as he was. He paused, got invested in what was going on and started helping me out. And all I could think about was why. What would he get out of this? Helping someone in need once is normal, but actually caring enough to stay and become invested in someone else’s life is another level of kindness, no?

I kept asking why because every kind of goodness I knew had a reason behind it. Sometimes, blood ties made it an obligation. Sometimes, it was transactional. Sometimes, the person helping wanted to feel better about themselves because they had helped someone else. Whatever the reason, there was always a reason. So when I came across love that didn’t need one, I got confused.

I didn’t trust it for as long as my doubt could survive. He never tried to convince me that his goodness came without a reason. He wasn’t bothered by my doubts at all. He was just being who he was. I kept waiting for the day I would have to do something in return, but that day never came. So I started making things happen on my own, trying to compensate for the love and kindness I was receiving.

Every time I did something, it felt so fake because it didn’t come from the abundance of life within me. It came from a need to relieve myself of the guilt of having to just sit and be loved. For free. I felt so undeserving. It was too much for a brain that only knew transactional love to comprehend. With every attempt to do something for him, I felt smaller and smaller before him and his love I could never live up to.

He didn’t do anything about it. He just kept loving me. Did I doubt him even after he had shown me he was for real? He never tried to explain himself. He just loved me until my doubts grew thin enough to be swayed away by the wind. Did I try to compensate by making things happen for him? He never got mad or anything. He just kept loving me until my attempts stood ashamed before his love. Did I feel bad for not doing enough? He kept loving me until I was convinced that I wasn’t the one who had to make this relationship possible. Did I feel small and insecure? He just showed up and loved me until I grew so big that the rooms I used to feel small in started to feel suffocating. Did I feel unclean and broken? His unwavering love stayed long enough for me to feel washed clean and mended.

You know, the worst thing about not being loved is not just the absence of love. It is how that absence convinces you that you are unlovable and teaches you to become hard and unreceptive to love. His love outlasted everything and rewrote everything that being unloved for so long had taught me. We’re now best friends. Or at least, I say so. Am I his best friend? I don’t know. But he is my best friend. He is the one I trust with everything. The first person I run to when I am sad. I once read a line that said “have you noticed we run to the people we love when we’re happy, but when we’re sad, we run to the people who love us?” and I instantly thought of him. The one person I will forever be sure loves me, no matter what.

It was a need for help that made me reach out to a stranger that first night. But that first time I reached out was only the beginning for me. I didn’t know Him until everything I had depended on ran dry, leaving me with nowhere else to turn. He has always been there, all I needed was to need him and reach out.
