But I wasn’t a stranger to Him. He knew me. The person I now call my best friend had known me all along. Even before the foundation of the world. Even before I came to be. 

And, as is typical of besties, this best friend of mine and I don’t have pictures together.

articles.title: Write about happiness
articles.highlight: joy feels quieter, more familiar and safer
articles.body:
Once, during an informal gathering, the question “what do you want to be in the future?” was given as an icebreaker. Me being me, I said “happy.” But today, I have a hard time defining what that happiness means. I guess hearing a word being thrown around so often or saying it yourself doesn’t necessarily mean you know what it exactly mean. I don’t know much about happiness, except it being the absence of sadness.

When I think about happiness, what naturally comes to mind is a place. A green one. Sort of a garden with beautiful flowers and plants and for some reason, the people there never stop smiling. It seems like a perfect place in my imaginary world. No inconveniences. No sad face, everyone just smiling all the time like they’re on ad. It feels unrealistic, like a place designed to sell me an idea of happiness rather than show me what it actually looks like.

Now, forcing myself to think harder about what happiness might be, it seems like a strange land. Somewhere new I have traveled to without knowing anything about it. The language is new to my ears, let alone one I can speak. The facial expressions of the strangers are impossible to interpret and I don’t know where or how to get back. Happiness is unfamiliar space and I am not good at dealing with unfamiliar things. I know sadness more closely than I know happiness, so my version of happiness has always been just being less sad.

I don’t know happiness, but I know something that looks like it. Joy. Both have something to do with contentment, with being where you are and not wishing to be somewhere else in that moment. But happiness feels like a loud celebration of that contentment, when joy feels quieter, more familiar and safer. When happiness feels like the absence of sadness, joy feels like moments of breaks in the sadness and growing to balance both. I feel like I understand joy better. It doesn't feel like a strange land I have to learn how to navigate. It feels like something I can recognize. The moments of joy don't look like the garden in my imagination. Nobody is smiling all the time and nothing about them is extraordinary. They feel real and that makes them easier for me to trust it.

When I said I wanted to be happy when I get old, I was imagining a life where sadness has only a little room to exist. A life where feeling okay didn't require so much effort. But I am beginning to wonder if happiness is less about being less sad and more about finding the courage to live with sadness without letting it become the only thing I know. And that courage comes from the small moments of joy that remind me there is more to life than what hurts. Like laughing so hard during a conversation that, for a moment, I forget about the thing I was worried about. The problems are still there when the laughter fades, but now they feel a little less like the whole world.

articles.title: The power of music
articles.highlight: move through different stages of our lives without moving our feet
articles.body:
I think music is one of the things that makes life make sense. It is our attempt to make sense of reality, recreate experiences, mourn losses, express desires, hold on to hope, worship and give shapes to things that might otherwise be difficult to express through sound, in a beautiful way. I love music. I love listening to music of course, but more than that, I love how people love music. How both the people who create it and those who listen to it become connected to it and make it part of themselves. I love that music is an art form of its own, with so many different forms, styles, and possibilities. I love that every piece of music carries something of the people who made it, whether a lesson, love, hurt, a memory or hope.

I like to think of music as a gift to humanity, something we were given so we could love ourselves with it, be friends with it and experience life a little more deeply. Sometimes, I wonder what life would be like without music. A world without the sound of musical instruments, without melodies, without people discovering that their voices could do more than speaking. Imagine never knowing that sounds could be arranged in such a way that they make you want to dance, cry, remember, or feel something you cannot name. Thank God that’s not how life is. Thank God music exists.

Music has been with humanity for as long as we have been making it. Over the years, it has changed alongside us, finding new forms through the advancement of technology. We have found new instruments, new ways to record, and new ways to share the music we love. And through all these changes, music has stayed with us, the only thing that has changed is the mediums we create and experience it with. It stayed with us because it is powerful.

And one of the powers of music is its ability to hold memories of places, people, and different periods of our lives, keeping them tucked away until we encounter a certain song again. Recently, I was sitting somewhere, waiting for my food, when I suddenly found myself seeing a version of me from a certain period of my life. The feeling that came with the memory was so unpleasant that it made me physically nauseous. I couldn't stop thinking about it, and it wasn't until I was about to leave that I realized what had triggered it. The classical music playing in the background of the restaurant was the same music I remembered from that moment in my life. I made me remember the experience so clearly that, for a moment, it felt as though I were experiencing them all over again. The music wasn’t intentionally chosen to accompany those events. It had just been playing in the background by coincidence, yet, my mind had kept it as an underscore to those memories, and hearing it again brought them all back.

I find that interesting. A music that exists independently of us, playing in rooms we enter and places we pass through becomes part of the experience silently. Years later, that same music will bring us face-to-face with a version of story we forgot, a person we miss, a place we cannot return to or a feeling we thought we had forgotten.  That is one of the power of music: it allows us to move through different stages of our lives without moving our feet. Through a song, we can revisit places we have left, people we have lost and moments that are no longer here. We can travel as far back as our memories and the music associated with them will take us.

articles.title: Favorite movie
articles.highlight: I think Rio is lovely.
articles.body:
First of all, don’t judge me when I say I’m not a movie person. Whenever I think about watching a movie, all I can think about is the commitment it requires, which I rarely am ready to make. As I’ve grown older, movies have become less and less fun for me, and watching them now takes up a very small part of my time.

In a way, I blame my brother for this. He traumatized me early in childhood by exposing me to too many horror and action movies before I was even old enough to understand what was going on. Because movies were such an important thing for him, the rest of us in the house rarely got to choose what to watch. We just watched whatever he wanted. So, at an age when I should have been watching cartoons, I was watching people beating the shit out of each other, someone discovering human flesh as a food source, and entire cities burning down every other minute. Mind you, I barely understood the plots most of the time. 

Sometimes, though, he watched cartoons. One of the cartoons I watched with him was Rio, the story of two blue macaws. I watched it so many times as a child because it was my favorite movie. I think it still is. About a month ago, I was watching it again and for a moment, I felt twelve all over again, watching with the same excitement, wishing I could be a bird (thinking how easy they have it). The two blue birds were Just so beautiful to my eyes. I doubt there’s any bird I could find more beautiful than them. The story is interesting and believable, and even though I’m usually impatient with the musical parts of animated movies, I enjoy watching the characters in rio sing.

I’m sure the reason why I loved Rio so much then was because I was a child. But even now as an adult, I can say beyond the nostalgia, it’s still such a fun movie. It reminds me of the importance of courage, stepping outside my comfort zone, friendships and being there for one another. It reminds me that surrounding myself with people who are like me can help me discover myself better, that I can be scared, and still make things happen, and that people from different backgrounds can share their lives as long as they are willing to make room for one another.

Beyond the lessons, it is such a joyful movie. The music, the colors, the characters and the two beautiful birds make it a world I enjoy returning to. I think Rio is lovely.

articles.title: Single and happy
articles.highlight: Single and content.
articles.body:
I don’t like this title, single and happy. Not because I’m single and unhappy, but because the title implies that being single and happy is somehow out of the ordinary. The assumption seems to be people are usually single and unhappy. I also hate the fact that that assumption is true. People are usually single and unhappy.

How do I know? Simply take the unhealthy amount of views and comments on any content related to relationships. I think people are too invested in it, which isn’t a bad thing in itself. But sometimes, it crosses the line into desperation and I think that’s why people are often unhappy about being single. Yes, it is unrealistic to be happy about singleness all the time. There will be days when you feel unhappy about it, there might be seasons when you really really hate it and there might be times you love it. But through all of this, I think one should find a way to be content about life.

I personally think I am single and content. Happiness can be a sign of contentment, but that’s not always the case. People usually say, “I’m single and happy” to say that they’re single by choice and I don’t really understand the concept of being single by choice. If someone decides never to get married, that’s singleness by choice. But saying you’re single by choice to mean “there are people who are interested in me, but I don’t want to be with them” doesn’t make sense to me. Because how many of those who are “single by choice” would choose to remain single after finding someone they’re mutually attracted to. If it’s about having someone interested, of course, many people have someone who wants them. Most people are single because they haven’t found their person and I don’t see the choice in that.  So, when I say I am single and happy, or content, I’m not saying I’m single by choice. I am not, I am single forced by life to wait on the time I will cross paths with my person. 

But I am content about it. I think I’m content because I’m a very realistic person. As much as I want to be an optimist, when it comes to relationships, what I focus on is the work it takes for two people to be together and maintain that relationship. You meet someone from a completely different upbringing, learn their way of life, teach them your way of loving and then compromise on some things to meet halfway. I can see the friction from here. And as a chronic procrastinator, I can’t help but be happy that singleness procrastinates all that for me.  Yes, there will be cute, romantic moments, but knowing me I know I’ll just sit and wait for those moments to pass so I can get to the working stage of the relationship and it kills my excitement. Also, most of the relationships I see around inspire me to remain single for a very long time, if not forever so…

I also like the thrill of not knowing whom I’ll end up with. It gives me the privilege of being as delusional as I want and wishing for different kinds of personalities every time. I like the possibility of life turning out differently depending on whom I imagine myself with. When you have someone you know you’ll end up with, your guesses about how life might turn out will be limited. Whether those guesses become true or not, your imagination will be influenced by what you know about yourself and the other person. I just like not knowing whom I’ll end up with and being creative with it is fun.

I’m not sure whether these points have made me content or whether I’ve noticed them because I’m content. Either way, I am content. When I say I’m content, I mean I’m also content with the possibility of my future. As someone who thinks about the worst scenario beforehand to spare myself the surprise of life, I think about ending up single forever, too. Because it is better than suffering together out of the fear of being alone. When I say I’m open to remaining single instead of ending up with the wrong person, relatively older people tell me, “you’ll change your mind”.  Maybe they’re right. I might. Especially when I see people compromise their most important values as they get older just to be with someone, I fear I might do the same. Because what makes me different? Who knows what kind of person I will be after two decades? 

That part shakes my contentment sometimes. But I hope and pray that will not be me. Because I know too much about what it means to be with the wrong person and I can’t afford it. After everything I’ve seen, I can’t afford to be with someone just for the sake of having someone in my life. I hope my person exists somewhere in the world and I get to meet and be with him one day. But if I’m destined to be single forever, I’m not going to force someone to be mine. And I hope I stick to this forever.

Single and content.

Amen.

articles.title: Your parents
articles.highlight: She happily said it was an honor.
articles.body:
My earliest memories of my parents are of them after life had made them tough. They were all about responsibility, rarely having fun, always discussing something serious. Because I was so used to seeing them being serious, I found it odd whenever they joked around and made fun of something. I also came to expect people to be serious and stressed by default. But that was just my assumption.

I think that assumption shaped how I saw parenthood, too. When I think about being a parent, the first thing that comes to mind is sacrifice. Extending yourself to your limits so your child can have the best of what you can provide. Always prioritizing this new mini you. I'm not sure whether that's because it's the only part of parenthood I know or whether that's all there is to know about being a parent.

So a few hours ago I asked my mom what being a parent was like for her. She happily said it was an honor. Of all the words in the world, I didn't expect that one at all. She talked for more than ten minutes about how it was the best thing that could happen to anyone. “ልጅ እኮ እግዚአብሔር በነፃ ስለሚሰጠን እንጂ እንዴት ያለ ውድ ነገር መሰለሽ” she kept saying. I even asked her whether she thought she had sacrificed too much, and she said she didn't feel like she had sacrificed at all.  I'm happy that she doesn't regret us, but why was all I ever saw the sacrifices and not the pride she took in being a mom? 

I have a weird relationship with everyone, including my parents and growing up was tough. For a long time, I assumed they were the problem. But now I’ve now grown enough to recognize that I wasn't always easy to deal with either and that I usually made things difficult for them. I guess growing up opens your eyes to your own problem, and as much as I used to feel annoyed with them, all I can see now is the love it took me forever to recognize.

I think part of what took me so long was that I always wanted them to love me the way I wanted to be loved. But people love differently. I think love is as diverse as the number of people in the world, and waiting until someone loves you in a way that makes sense to your own language of love might mean missing out on the experience altogether. My parents either didn't have the resources or didn't know how to love me in the ways I needed to be loved. Whatever they had, though, they gave us all of it.

The more I understand them as people, the more grateful I feel for everything they've done to raise me. Did I have the best childhood? No. But I was loved and prioritized. Do I think my parents are perfect? Far from it. But they tried their best, and I know what it feels like when your best isn't enough. So the least I can do is see the effort behind things I once thought were not enough and appreciate it. I am grateful.

articles.title: Places you want to visit
articles.highlight: I don't want to visit places, I want to live there for a while.
articles.body:
የማያውቁት ሀገር አይናፍቅም ከሚሉት መካከል ነኝ። እንኳን የማያውቁት፣ የሚያውቁትም አይናፍቅም ባይ። When I see a place on internet, rarely do think about going there to visit. I usually read about them, look at pictures, admire the beauty of the cities, check the value of their currencies and that’s pretty much it. I didn’t grow up dreaming about visiting places, but then I grew up and realized that everyone wants to travel and see the world. So I added traveling to my list because,if everyone wants it must be good, no?  

But to be honest, እኔ መሄድ አልወድም። The act of going somewhere new doesn’t appeal to me as much as it seems to appeal to other people. It feels like a responsibility that takes away from the fun. Not to mention having to figure things out in a new place, explore, and walk nonstop. I just don’t think the tourist life is for me.  What is for me, though, is moving to different places every year or two and live there. I would do anything for that kind of lifestyle. 

Maybe it’s because I have little to no experience traveling and I need to experience before I can have an opinion. But travelling for just two weeks is stressful for my nervous system that needs more than two weeks to feel safe and sleep properly in a new environment. I don't want to visit places, I want to live there for a while. But then again, I shouldn’t have an opinion on something I haven’t really experienced. That said, there are a few places I have in mind, mostly inspired by things I’ve seen on the internet.

Edinburgh: I think I loved Edinburgh after coming across a picture of the city on Facebook many years ago. I instantly loved it, searched for more pictures on Google and said to myself, “I’ll go there one day". I can’t explain why I chose Edinburgh when there are so many other cities just as beautiful, but for some reason, it’s the only city I’ve ever made up my mind to visit.

Seattle: There was a season in my life that I read a lot of romance and there was this one book (I will not mention it because you’ll know it and judge me) set in Seattle. It painted such a perfect picture of the city in my head that I now feel the need to go there and see if the real place is close to what I’ve imagined.

Maldives: Because everytime I see pictures from someone who went to Maldives, the place gives off it was created for people who want to do nothing and have fun while doing nothing.

Asmara: I’ve watched multiple travel vlogs in Asmara and the city always leaves me with a feeling I can’t quite put into words and I feel like going there will help me understand what exactly it is that feeling.

Italy: I have a picture I screenshotted from internet that I want to recreate with my best friend 😂️️

New York: I’ve watched so many living in New York vlogs that I feel like I owe it to myself to take myself out on a solo coffee date there.

articles.title: A memory
articles.highlight: so that I can love people longer
articles.body:
I used to struggle a lot with confrontation. The kind of people pleaser I was mostly came from my inability to deal with chaos and disagreements because I had no experience of people dealing with disagreements peacefully. For me, disagreeing meant eternal separation, so I conditioned myself to be okay with everything happening, whether I liked it or not.

The thing about being a people pleaser, you know this if you ever were one, is that the peace you've neglected yourself for during the day will haunt you at night as chaos. Every yes to things you didn't really want but went along with anyway will make you feel small and betrayed. Because you're supposed to care about what matters to you just as much as you're invested in the peace you're building alone in a two or more person relationship. So every time I said yes when I wanted to say no, my heart grew a little colder towards the other person, as if the choice I made was their fault. Resentment and withdrawal were the only compensation worth the grief of not being able to show up for myself.

I have this funny story about getting into a conflict with someone I loved after I noticed this pattern. 

She did things that hurt me at the time, after a week of feeling so off about her, I realized I had to talk to this person about what was going on, or I would grow to resent her. And she meant too much to me for me to just easily go cold without trying. So, for the very first time, I decided to confront her and tell her what was going on from my side. My assumption was that I might panic a little because I had never done that before, but since she loves me, she would easily understand me, we would work on the issue and be okay.

I procrastinated on the day I would talk to her because it was stressful. I thought about every word I would say, rehearsing the lines as if they wouldn't get lost in the vapor the moment I started the conversation. After almost two weeks of overthinking it, there we were, sitting down to talk because I told her I had something to tell her. Only a minute into the conversation, the air got thick, I was panicking, sweating and couldn't say a thing, so I started crying. This wasn't me at 13 or 17, by the way. This was me, almost 22. A grown adult with responsibilities, crying like I had just learned of the loss of someone I loved because I couldn't say, "You hurt my feelings when you said or did this.” I couldn't stop crying. It was so dramatic. She was very patient, but I just couldn't get to my point that at one point she said "ምንም ራሱ እየተፈጠረ አይደለም, ምንድነው የሚያስለቅስሽ?" Yes, nothing was happening, but I just couldn't soothe myself.

So I finally did talk and the response was funny. I thought it was a big deal because it was a big deal for me, and I was attempting to fix what had happened. I thought she'd understand me and take me seriously too. She didn't. The response was so cold that I still laugh a little when I think about it. The whole scenario was funny. The humiliation of it all. With a face that seemed to say ‘all this crying for this, you waster of tears?’ she said, "I think you're too sensitive and childish. It's like I have to be conscious of every interaction as if I'm dealing with a child, and I am sorry but I'm too busy to care at that level right now.”

What???

I instantly stopped crying as whatever sense of safety I has with her evaporated into the roof above us. I regretted it.

Not the act of speaking up, because it was my first time I ever said ‘stop doing this because this is hurting me.’ And starting with that, I eventually learned to speak my side little by little. I now know that confronting someone isn't that big of a deal. I can do it easily when necessary so that I can love people longer. So, it was a win in that side.

What I regretted, though, is the weeks I spent overthinking every single line because I didn't want to come off as insensitive and hurt her. The stress I went through, only to be met with something that didn't even have a hint of care for my feelings. The tears I cried because my nervous system thought I might lose this relationship, only to be met with, ‘you're too sensitive.’

I still regret that part.

_*I really wanted to write about something happier, but, the opposite happened to be more interesting and easier to reach and put into words.*_

articles.title: Things that makes you happy
articles.highlight: Rereading a sentence again and again because it’s beautiful
articles.body:
1. Mornings (especially after a good night sleep)
2. Colors 
3. The smell of coffee
4. Notebooks 
5. Deep conversations 
6. Learning something new about God
7. Learning something new about humans
8. A simple act of consideration 
9. Ye Akko fasting beyaynet 
10. My friends offensive joke about poverty
11. My sisters perfume choice 
12. Goofing around 
13. Watching vlogs
14. Seeing my friends get excited
15. Reading someone's personal reflections
16. Hearing someone talk passionately about something they love
17. Make up
18. Creative things  
19. Words
20. Baggy jeans
21. Old photographs
22. Trees
23. Avocados with pretty privilege
24. Being silly with my friends
25. A quiet time with God
26. Crossing things off a to do list
27. The moment of getting into bed when I'm exhausted
28. When an unplanned outfit turns out perfect
29. Hanging out with my sister
30. Seeing peoples handwriting
31. Getting ready to go to a wedding 
32. Finding money I forgot I had 
33. Having nothing urgent to do
34. Good packaging
35. Rereading a sentence again and again because it’s beautiful
36. Seeing old couples care for one another
37. Discovering a YouTube channel I love and binge watching all their videos
38. Hearing peoples testimony
39. Seeing someone laugh uncontrollably
40. Keeping promises I made to myself

I can't believe when I'm not in a good place in life, I have such a hard time remembering any of these things and focus on having nothing to be happy about in life. I think when I feel down next time, I should come to this list and try doing some of these things. 

Also, I highly recommend making a list of things that make you happy. It's such a fun way to explore yourself and you'll have a list to come back to on the days when happiness feels a little far to be reached.
